places.quote: “A capitalist,—an Insurer of Ships.” I suppose he saw me glancing about the room in search of some tokens of Shipping, or capital, for he added, “In the City.”
places.note: Financial district of London, named by Herbert.

places.quote: Yet in the London streets so crowded with people and so brilliantly lighted in the dusk of evening
places.note: City as a whole; no specific street named.

places.quote: next day we went to church at Westminster Abbey
in the afternoon we walked in the Parks
places.note: Unnamed; likely Hyde Park or another London park.

places.quote: the footsteps of some incapable impostor of a porter mooning about Barnard’s Inn
places.note: Where Pip and Herbert lodge; Inn of Chancery.

places.quote: He was to come away in an hour or two to attend me to Hammersmith
places.note: Then a Middlesex village on London's western edge.

places.quote: I think I shall trade,” said he, leaning back in his chair, “to the East Indies, for silks, shawls, spices, dyes, drugs, and precious woods.
“I think I shall trade, also,” said he, putting his thumbs in his waist-coat pockets, “to the West Indies, for sugar, tobacco, and rum.
Also to Ceylon, especially for elephants’ tusks.
